lines.text: We forecast Wiwynn’s September sales to be NT$85.0bn (-11% MoM, +146% YoY)
thanks to stronger-than-expected shipments of racks for AWS ASICs. While the
market has been concerned about the AWS ASIC transition period starting from
4Q25, we believe robust demand for CSP clients’ regular servers and the ramp-up
for Oracle’s GPU rack demand could mitigate this. We expect Wiwynn’s Mexico
facility to support Oracle’s GPU rack demand, and its upcoming US plant will
further support AWS ASIC liquid cooling rack manufacturing from 2H26. We lift
25-27CT EPS by 6-18% and raise our TP from NT$3,600 to NT$4,200. Maintain
Driven by increased cloud Capex, Wiwynn as the major AWS ASIC L10/L11 supplier
has continued to benefit from ASIC demand. With ongoing robust shipments for
AWS Trainium2, we forecast September sales of NT$85.0bn, -11% MoM, +146%
YoY, thanks to the robust demand for AWS ASICs, and this will lead to 3Q25CT
revenue of NT$266bn, which is 17% higher than consensus forecasts.
AWS ASIC transition impact could be mitigated
While the market has been concerned about the period of AWS’ ASIC transition
from Trainium2 to Trainium3, we believe Wiwynn has two strong catalysts to
mitigate any impact: regular servers and Oracle AI servers. We see continued
strength in CSP regular server demand into 4Q25. And for Oracle’s orders,
Wiwynn’s Mexico plant could facilitate manufacturing from L10/L11. We expect
the revenue contribution from Oracle to begin from 4Q25 and reach 5% into 2026
As new US capacity comes online in end-4Q25/early-1Q26, Wiwynn will complete
the manufacturing support for key customers’ AI server demand under the current
uncertain US tariff conditions. Its US plant will focus on production of liquid cooling
server racks, in line with the trend of ASIC liquid cooling adoption from 4Q25
onwards. Into 2026, with AWS’ rising ASIC demand for Trainium3 and ongoing order
share wins in GPU racks, we forecast 2026 sales to grow 10% YoY.
We lift 25/26/27CT EPS by 6%/14%/18% to reflect the strong near-term demand
from AWS Trainium2, higher revenue contribution from AWS Trainium3 and
Oracle’s GPU server shipments, resulting in a higher TP of NT$4,200 (from

Our target price is based on a PE valuation methodology as we believe it better
reflects market expectations for the company’s earnings growth outlook. Our target

contribution. We believe a 16x PE is justified given its 51% EPS Cagr over 24-27CT.

body.text: With ongoing robust shipments for AWS Trainium2, we forecast September sales of NT$85.0bn, -11% MoM, +146% YoY, thanks to the robust demand for AWS ASICs, and this will lead to 3Q25CT revenue of NT$266bn, which is 17% higher than consensus forecasts.
body.title: Outperform.

body.text: AWS ASIC transition impact could be mitigated While the market has been concerned about the period of AWS’ ASIC transition from Trainium2 to Trainium3, we believe Wiwynn has two strong catalysts to mitigate any impact: regular servers and Oracle AI servers.
body.title: Outperform.

body.text: We see continued strength in CSP regular server demand into 4Q25.
body.title: Outperform.

body.text: And for Oracle’s orders, Wiwynn’s Mexico plant could facilitate manufacturing from L10/L11.
body.title: Outperform.

body.text: We expect the revenue contribution from Oracle to begin from 4Q25 and reach 5% into 2026 with upside risk.
body.title: Outperform.

body.text: Stronger 2026 outlook As new US capacity comes online in end-4Q25/early-1Q26, Wiwynn will complete the manufacturing support for key customers’ AI server demand under the current uncertain US tariff conditions.
body.title: Outperform.

body.text: Its US plant will focus on production of liquid cooling server racks, in line with the trend of ASIC liquid cooling adoption from 4Q25 onwards.
body.title: Outperform.

body.text: Into 2026, with AWS’ rising ASIC demand for Trainium3 and ongoing order share wins in GPU racks, we forecast 2026 sales to grow 10% YoY.
body.title: Outperform.

body.text: Earnings revisions and valuation We lift 25/26/27CT EPS by 6%/14%/18% to reflect the strong near-term demand from AWS Trainium2, higher revenue contribution from AWS Trainium3 and Oracle’s GPU server shipments, resulting in a higher TP of NT$4,200 (from NT$3,600), still based on 16x 26CT PE.

thanks to stronger-than-expected shipments of racks for AWS ASICs. While the 
market has been concerned about the AWS ASIC transition period starting from 
4Q25, we believe robust demand for CSP clients’ regular servers and the ramp-up
for Oracle’s GPU rack demand could mitigate this. We expect Wiwynn’s Mexico 
facility to support Oracle’s GPU rack demand, and its upcoming US plant will 
further support AWS ASIC liquid cooling rack manufacturing from 2H26. We lift 
25-27CT EPS by 6-18% and raise our TP from NT$3,600 to NT$4,200. Maintain 
Outperform.

We forecast Wiwynn’s September sales to be NT$85.0bn (-11% MoM, +146% YoY) 
thanks to stronger-than-expected shipments of racks for AWS ASICs. While the 
market has been concerned about the AWS ASIC transition period starting from 
4Q25, we believe robust demand for CSP clients’ regular servers and the ramp-up
for Oracle’s GPU rack demand could mitigate this. We expect Wiwynn’s Mexico 
facility to support Oracle’s GPU rack demand, and its upcoming US plant will 
further support AWS ASIC liquid cooling rack manufacturing from 2H26. We lift 
25-27CT EPS by 6-18% and raise our TP from NT$3,600 to NT$4,200. Maintain 
Outperform.

a more subdued revenue outlook; 2) intensifying competition in datacentre

Risks include 1) a slowdown in CSP clients’ Capex investment, which could lead to
a more subdued revenue outlook; 2) intensifying competition in datacentre
hardware that may result in order loss and/or margin pressure; 3) slower-than-
expected ramp-up of new business development, especially in new client and AI
penetration, that could lead to a more volatile earnings profile; and 4) short supply
of key components that would impede the schedule for product shipments and the
revenue outlook.

source_guided_digest.source_heading: AWS ASIC transition impact could be mitigated
source_guided_digest.text: While the market has been concerned about the period of AWS’ ASIC transition from Trainium2 to Trainium3, we believe Wiwynn has two strong catalysts to mitigate any impact: regular servers and Oracle AI servers. We see continued strength in CSP regular server demand into 4Q25. And for Oracle’s orders, Wiwynn’s Mexico plant could facilitate manufacturing from L10/L11. We expect the revenue contribution from Oracle to begin from 4Q25 and reach 5% into 2026 with upside risk.

Expect better-than-feared 4Q25 and promising 2026 outlook
We forecast Wiwynn’s September sales to be NT$85.0bn (-11% MoM, +146% YoY) thanks to stronger-than-expected shipments of racks for AWS ASICs.
While the market has been concerned about the AWS ASIC transition period starting from 4Q25, we believe robust demand for CSP clients’ regular servers and the ramp-up for Oracle’s GPU rack demand could mitigate this.
We expect Wiwynn’s Mexico facility to support Oracle’s GPU rack demand, and its upcoming US plant will further support AWS ASIC liquid cooling rack manufacturing from 2H26.
We lift 25-27CT EPS by 6-18% and raise our TP from NT$3,600 to NT$4,200.
Maintain Outperform.
3Q25 preview
Driven by increased cloud Capex, Wiwynn as the major AWS ASIC L10/L11 supplier has continued to benefit from ASIC demand.
With ongoing robust shipments for AWS Trainium2, we forecast September sales of NT$85.0bn, -11% MoM, +146% YoY, thanks to the robust demand for AWS ASICs, and this will lead to 3Q25CT revenue of NT$266bn, which is 17% higher than consensus forecasts.
AWS ASIC transition impact could be mitigated
While the market has been concerned about the period of AWS’ ASIC transition from Trainium2 to Trainium3, we believe Wiwynn has two strong catalysts to mitigate any impact: regular servers and Oracle AI servers.
We see continued strength in CSP regular server demand into 4Q25.
And for Oracle’s orders, Wiwynn’s Mexico plant could facilitate manufacturing from L10/L11.
We expect the revenue contribution from Oracle to begin from 4Q25 and reach 5% into 2026 with upside risk.
Stronger 2026 outlook
As new US capacity comes online in end-4Q25/early-1Q26, Wiwynn will complete the manufacturing support for key customers’ AI server demand under the current uncertain US tariff conditions.
Its US plant will focus on production of liquid cooling server racks, in line with the trend of ASIC liquid cooling adoption from 4Q25 onwards.
Into 2026, with AWS’ rising ASIC demand for Trainium3 and ongoing order share wins in GPU racks, we forecast 2026 sales to grow 10% YoY.
Earnings revisions and valuation
We lift 25/26/27CT EPS by 6%/14%/18% to reflect the strong near-term demand from AWS Trainium2, higher revenue contribution from AWS Trainium3 and Oracle’s GPU server shipments, resulting in a higher TP of NT$4,200 (from NT$3,600), still based on 16x 26CT PE.
Maintain Outperform.
Investment thesis
Expect it to benefit from strong CSP ASIC server demand in 2025; new server platform ramp-ups and accelerating ASIC server shipments.
Risk-reward looks favourable even if there is no AI contribution from the Middle East.
Catalysts
1) Stronger-than-expected ASIC server demand; 2) faster-than-expected general server shipment ramp-up; 3) better-than-expected Middle East contribution.
Valuation details
Our target price is based on a PE valuation methodology as we believe it better reflects market expectations for the company’s earnings growth outlook.
Our target price is based on 16x 2026CT PE, 1sd above the five-year average PE, to factor in stronger AI and ASIC server demand despite the removal of the Middle East contribution.
We believe a 16x PE is justified given its 51% EPS Cagr over 24-27CT.
Investment risks
Risks include 1) a slowdown in CSP clients’ Capex investment, which could lead to a more subdued revenue outlook; 2) intensifying competition in datacentre hardware that may result in order loss and/or margin pressure; 3) slower-than-expected ramp-up of new business development, especially in new client and AI penetration, that could lead to a more volatile earnings profile; and 4) short supply of key components that would impede the schedule for product shipments and the revenue outlook.
